column5: The turtle can pull its head inside it. => Many turtles can pull their heads inside it.
Look for an animal that can fly or lays eggs. => Look for an animal with wings and a beak.
Hens, snakes and butterflies lay eggs. => Hens, butterflies and most snakes lay eggs.
It has no feathers and lays its eggs in water. => It has no feathers, and most frogs lay their eggs in water.
and animals need plants for food. => and many animals eat plants.
Moon is for the night. => The Moon does not make heat.
Moon and stars are for the night. => We can see the Moon and stars at night.
Then comes the afternoon => Then come the afternoon
Adults are taller than children. => Adults are usually taller than children.
Pets like cats have babies in a nest. => Kittens and puppies grow inside their mothers.
What do the baby rabbits grow after three weeks? => What do the baby rabbits have after three weeks?
The baby rabbits grow soft fur after three weeks. => The baby rabbits have soft fur after three weeks.
A snake lives on land. => A snake never grows legs.
Fish, frogs and water plants are living things that live in water. => Fish and water plants live in water. Frogs live in water and on land.
A toy car moves only when someone pushes it. => A toy car moves only when it is pushed or has a battery.
Metal things sink. => Coins and metal spoons sink.
Metal things sink. => Small metal things, like a key, sink.
Light things float. => Feathers and leaves stay on top of the water.
A stone is heavy. => A stone is heavy for its size.
The plastic stays dry. => The water runs off the plastic.
Which material stays dry? => Which material keeps the water out?
Plastic stays dry, so it is best for an umbrella. => Water runs off plastic, so it is best for an umbrella.
Which one stays dry? => Which one stays dry inside?
A plastic cup will not break if it falls. => A plastic cup does not usually break if it falls.
Metal is too heavy for a pencil. => A metal pencil would be hard to sharpen.
Metal things are hard and cold. => Metal things are hard and often feel cold.
Glass breaks if you drop it. => Glass can break if you drop it.
Spoons and keys are metal. => Spoons and keys can be metal.
Pencil cases are made of cloth or plastic. => Pencil cases are usually made of cloth or plastic.
You pull it back toward you. => You pull it back towards you.
toward you => towards you
Something must push or kick it. => Something must push or pull it.
Think about the four tastes your tongue can notice. => Think about the tastes your tongue can notice.
It starts with e. => It is not the eye or the nose.
It is on the middle of your face. => It is in the middle of your face.
Loud sounds hurt your ears. => Very loud sounds can hurt your ears.

Toast burns for ever. It cannot go back into bread. => Burnt toast is changed for ever. It cannot go back into bread.
turning a jar lid => turning the ends of a pipe cleaner
Heat melts things. => Heat melts chocolate.
At midday it is overhead. => At midday it is high in the sky.
Read the middle sentence. => Read the sentence about noon.
The Sun stays still in this idea. => The Sun only seems to move.
Things that use electricity need a plug or batteries. => Things that use electricity often have a plug or batteries.
It runs out when it is old. => It runs out after a lot of use.
Toys need batteries. => Many toys that move by themselves use batteries.
It is at the start. => You put one in a torch.
A thermometer measures heat. => A thermometer measures temperature.
To compare two paper planes fairly, => To compare two paper plane shapes fairly,
Grips do not change weight. => Grips do not make shoes lighter.
Deep sand is very rough. => Wheels sink into deep sand.
Pull means toward. => Pull means towards.
A pull moves things toward you. => A pull moves things towards you.
Orangutans live in the trees. They do not swim in the sea. => Rainforest monkeys live in the trees. They do not need the sea.
A penguin lives where it is very cold. => A polar bear lives where it is very cold.
a penguin in the cold Arctic. => a polar bear in the cold Arctic.
It looks like the leaf, so hunters do not see it. => Its colour matches the leaf, so hunters may not see it.
It comes from a tap. => It is clear and has no colour.
Fruit grows on trees. => Fruit grows on plants.
Soap kills germs. => Soap washes germs away.
Mia drank 6 glasses on Monday, => The table shows 6 glasses on Monday,
Every plant starts from something small in the soil. => A plant can start from something small in the soil.
Mammals are born alive. => Most mammals are born alive.
when the Sun is far away. => when our side of the Earth faces away from the Sun.
Everyone is asleep. => Most people are asleep.
That is why shadows have sharp edges. => That is why light does not go round an object, and a shadow forms behind it.
Choose the solid one. => Choose the one you cannot see through.
Solid things make shadows. => Things you cannot see through make shadows.
It grows, so it is alive. => It feeds and grows, so it is alive.
Things that grow are alive. => A mushroom feeds and grows.
Mushrooms grow, so they are alive. => Mushrooms feed and grow, so they are alive.
A wooden table is once alive because wood comes from a tree. => A wooden table is made from something once alive, because wood comes from a tree.
A pebble is once alive. => A pebble was once alive.
A dead leaf is once alive. => A dead leaf was once alive.
Now it is dead, so it is once alive. => Now it is dead, so we say it was once alive.
Plants are not alive without the things they need. => Plants cannot stay alive without the things they need.
Dry things cannot grow. => A dry seed cannot start to grow.
Wind does not give energy. => Wind does not give a plant energy to make food.
Stones do not give energy. => Stones do not give a plant energy to make food.
Sound does not give energy. => Sound does not give a plant energy to make food.
Rocks such as granite and stone are hard and strong. => Rocks such as granite and limestone are hard and strong.
It comes before thunder. => We see it before we hear the thunder.
A storm has thunder, lightning and heavy rain. => A storm can have thunder, lightning and heavy rain.
Winter has snow. => Winter can have snow.
What do we use to measure heat? => What do we use to measure how hot it is?
